passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS (“MD&A”) Performance Targets and Key Measures We target a total return of 12% to 15%+ per annum on the infrastructure assets that we own, measured over the long term. We intend to generate this return from the in-place cash flows from our operations plus growth through investments in upgrades and expansions of our asset base, as well as acquisitions. We determine our distributions to unitholders based primarily on an assessment of our operating performance. Funds From Operations (“FFO”) is used to assess our operating performance and can be used on a per unit basis as a proxy for future distribution growth over the long term. In addition, we have performance measures that track the key value drivers for each of our operating segments. See the “Segmented Disclosures” section of this MD&A for more detail. Performance Measures Used by Management To measure performance, we focus on net income, an IFRS Accounting Standards measure, as well as certain non-IFRS measures, including FFO, Adjusted Funds from Operations (“AFFO”), adjusted EBITDA (“Adjusted EBITDA”) and invested capital (“Invested Capital”), along with other measures. FFO We define FFO as net income excluding the impact of certain non-cash items including depreciation and amortization, deferred income taxes, mark-to-market gains (losses) and other income (expenses) that are not related to normal revenue earning activities or that are not normal, recurring cash operating expenses necessary for business operations. FFO is not adjusted for the income (loss) earned by data center developers which is generated through the development, commercialization, and sale of completed sites. The inclusion of this income reflects the operating performance of such investments and includes income (or losses) recognized in the current and prior periods. FFO also includes balances attributable to the partnership generated by investments in associates and joint ventures accounted for using the equity method and excludes amounts attributable to non-controlling interests based on the economic interests held by non-controlling interests in consolidated subsidiaries. Brookfield Infrastructure 111 FFO is a measure of operating performance that is not calculated in accordance with, and does not have any standardized meaning prescribed by IFRS. FFO is therefore unlikely to be comparable to similar measures presented by other issuers. FFO has limitations as an analytical tool. Specifically, our definition of FFO may differ from the definition used by other organizations, and is different than the definition of Funds from Operations used by the Real Property Association of Canada (“REALPAC”) and the National Association of Real Estate Investment Trusts, Inc. (“NAREIT”), in part because the NAREIT definition is based on U.S. GAAP, as opposed to IFRS. AFFO We define AFFO as FFO less capital expenditures required to maintain the current performance of our operations (maintenance capital expenditures). passages.heading: Debt note
passages.text: (a) Corporate Borrowings Brookfield Infrastructure has a $ 2.2 billion senior unsecured revolving credit facility used for general working capital purposes including acquisitions. The $ 2.2 billion is available on a revolving basis for the full term of the facility. All amounts outstanding under this facility will be repayable on June 29, 2030. All obligations of Brookfield Infrastructure under the facility are guaranteed by our partnership. Loans under this facility accrue interest at a floating rate based on SOFR plus 1.3 %. Brookfield Infrastructure is required to pay an unused commitment fee under the facility of 13 basis points per annum. As at December 31, 2025, there were $ nil (2024: $ 300 million) draws outstanding on the credit facility and $ 11 million of letters of credit were issued (2024: $ 10 million). credit_strengths.text: Operating margin expanded year over year and sits well above the sector median, reflecting the contracted, regulated-like economics of the issuer's infrastructure asset base across utilities, transport and midstream.

Operating cash flow grew strongly across the three-year trend, outpacing revenue growth and providing a substantial recurring cash base from which the partnership funds maintenance capital and distributions.

key_risks.text: Interest coverage improved only marginally year over year and remains far below the sector median, so operating income covers gross interest expense by a thin margin; the partnership's leveraged structure leaves little cushion against rate resets.

The debt note shows meaningful near-term refinancing: commercial paper matures within the year and medium-term notes fall due across the following years, while the revolver matures later; refinancing depends on continued market access at acceptable spreads.

Free cash flow is negative after capital expenditure, and acquisition spending is large relative to internally generated cash, so growth investment and distributions rely on external financing rather than retained cash flow.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Cash flow coverage of debt cannot be assessed because the balance sheet carries no tagged borrowings; the debt note discloses corporate borrowings and notes, so the missing debt metric is a material data gap for leverage and coverage analysis.
Liquidity is adequate but tight: the current ratio is below one, below the prior year and below the sector median, with cash and equivalents providing a modest buffer against current liabilities.

overall_credit_view.text: The issuer is a large, diversified infrastructure partnership with high margins and growing operating cash flow, but its indicative financial risk profile cannot be scored because borrowings are not tagged; leverage versus the sector median remains unknown pending confirmation from the debt note.

Analyst judgement: credit quality hinges on refinancing the disclosed note maturities and on converting strong operating cash flow into positive free cash flow; until then, distributions and acquisitions are funded externally and coverage headroom stays thin relative to peers.

credit_strengths.text: 經營利潤率按年擴大，並顯著高於行業中位數，反映發行人的基礎設施資產組合橫跨公用事業、運輸及中游業務，具有合約化、類監管式的經濟特徵。
經營現金流在三年趨勢中強勁增長，增速快於收入增長，提供龐大的經常性現金基礎，合夥企業藉此撥付維護性資本開支及分派。

key_risks.text: 利息覆蓋率按年僅輕微改善，且仍遠低於行業中位數，經營溢利對總利息開支的覆蓋幅度單薄；合夥企業的槓桿結構在利率重設下幾無緩衝。
債務附註顯示短期內有可觀的再融資需求：商業票據於年內到期，中期票據於隨後數年陸續到期，而循環信貸則較後到期；再融資取決於能否以可接受的息差持續進入市場。
資本開支後自由現金流為負，且收購支出相對內部產生現金而言規模龐大，故增長投資及分派依賴外部融資而非留存現金流。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 無法評估現金流對債務的覆蓋，因資產負債表並無標記借款；債務附註披露公司借款及票據，故缺失的債務指標對槓桿及覆蓋分析構成重大數據缺口。
流動性充足但偏緊：流動比率低於一，低於上年及行業中位數，現金及等價物對流動負債僅提供有限緩衝。

overall_credit_view.text: 發行人為大型多元化基礎設施合夥企業，利潤率高且經營現金流增長，但因其借款並無標記，無法就指示性財務風險狀況評分；相對行業中位數的槓桿水平仍有待債務附註確認。
分析師判斷：信貸質素取決於能否為所披露的票據到期進行再融資，以及能否將強勁經營現金流轉化為正自由現金流；在此之前，分派及收購均靠外部融資，覆蓋緩衝相對同業仍然單薄。
